AI Compass

Free AI lesson plans for teachers: 15 ready lessons with worksheets

Fifteen ready lessons about AI. Each plan has objectives, a warm-up, an activity, discussion questions and an exit ticket. The printable worksheet and its answer key are in the teacher kit of the app.

🌱 Basics

  1. Lesson plan: What is AI?explain in their own words what AI is; tell a program that follows hand-written rules from a system that learned from examples; explain why all AI today is narrow, and what general AI (AGI) would be.
  2. Lesson plan: Machine Learningexplain how machine learning differs from writing rules by hand; describe training (guess, measure the error, adjust, repeat) and explain why a model is tested on new examples; tell supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning apart, and explain why the data matters.
  3. Lesson plan: Neural Networksdescribe a neural network as many simple artificial neurons arranged in layers; explain what one neuron does with its inputs, weights, bias and activation function; explain that learning means adjusting the weights, little by little, to make the error smaller.
  4. Lesson plan: Generative AI & Chatbotsexplain that generative AI creates new content, and give examples; describe how a large language model writes: it predicts the next token, again and again; explain what a hallucination is, and use chatbots wisely: check the facts and keep personal data private.
  5. Lesson plan: AI in Everyday Lifefind the AI hidden in everyday apps and devices; explain how a recommendation system learns from what you watch, like and skip; explain what a filter bubble is, and name ways to stay in control of a feed.
  6. Lesson plan: AI Ethics & Safetyexplain how AI can learn bias from its data, with a real example; check a suspicious video or picture before sharing it; protect their privacy when using AI tools, and explain why people stay responsible for decisions made with AI.

🤿 Deep dive

  1. Lesson plan: How Computers Seeexplain how a picture becomes a grid of numbers (pixels, greyscale and RGB); describe how a filter slides over a picture to find edges (a convolution); explain how a CNN builds up from edges to objects, and why vision models can be fooled.
  2. Lesson plan: Learning by Trial and Errordescribe reinforcement learning with the words agent, environment, action and reward; explain the balance between exploration and exploitation, with an everyday example; explain how an agent learns what each move is worth, and what reward hacking is.
  3. Lesson plan: How Chatbots Writeexplain how text becomes tokens, and tokens become numbers; describe next-token prediction, and how temperature changes the choice of the next word; explain what attention does, and why a chatbot can sound sure and still be wrong.
  4. Lesson plan: Creative AIexplain that generative AI learns patterns from examples and uses them to make something new; describe, as an intuition, how a diffusion model turns noise into a picture, step by step; discuss consent, copyright, labels and deepfakes, and use AI as an honest creative partner.
  5. Lesson plan: Can You Trust AI?name three ways AI goes wrong: bias, hallucination and overconfidence; explain why one accuracy number is not enough, and how testing by group and red teaming help; protect their own data, and describe how laws such as the EU AI Act sort AI uses by risk.
  6. Lesson plan: Your AI Toolkitwrite a good prompt with a role, context, a clear task, an example and a format; check an AI answer: open the sources, compare with trusted ones, and notice when it sounds too sure; use AI as a tutor, not a ghostwriter, and explain why doing the thinking yourself matters.

🌍 AI in your world

  1. Lesson plan: Data: The Fuel of AIexplain where training data and labels come from, including the people who label it; find common problems in a dataset (missing, wrong, repeated and impossible values) and say why they matter; explain why a model is tested on a test set it never learned from, and recognise overfitting.
  2. Lesson plan: How Apps Choose for Youexplain what a recommendation system does and name its two big ideas (more of the same, people like you); list signals an app reads, and explain why actions say more than likes; explain how a filter bubble forms, and name at least three ways to widen their own feed.
  3. Lesson plan: Plan Your Own AI Projectdecide whether a problem needs AI or a simple rule; plan the data for a project: varied examples of every answer, with correct labels, and a test set; explain why one accuracy score isn't enough, and how to be honest with users about a model's limits.

The printable worksheet, its answer key and a classroom quiz for this lesson are in the teacher kit. Free, no sign-up.
